page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a custom arm64 Alibaba Yitian 710 processor operating at 2.75 GHz. It features 4 dedicated physical CPU cores with 1 thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 64 MB L3 cache per socket. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware networking provides 3 Gbps of baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no dedicated GPU accelerators and zero local NVMe storage, relying on network storage volumes.

Benchmark results show average performance across general and compute tasks. Multi-core CPU testing via stress-ng recorded 7235.59 points, with single-core performance reaching 1818.58 points. Memory throughput benchmarks recorded an uncached read bandwidth of 74.83 GB/sec and a cached read bandwidth of 408.75 GB/sec. Application testing showed steady throughput, logging 6.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.85 GB/sec during static web serving tests. However, instruction-heavy encryption tasks scored low on PassMark at 651.04 points due to the absence of x86-specific vector extensions. Inference tasks on small 135M LLM models achieved 128.91 tokens/sec for generation, dropping to 4.69 tokens/sec on 7B models.

The arm64 architectural efficiency of the Yitian 710 processor delivers strong qualitative cost effectiveness for workloads optimized for Arm instruction sets. With predictable dedicated CPU execution and standard network capacity, this server type is suitable for microservices, web serving, CI/CD worker nodes, and background ETL tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an arm64 Alibaba Yitian 710 processor running at 2.75 GHz. It offers 4 dedicated physical cores with 4 vCPUs, 8.0 GB of memory, and 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmarks, it exhibits mid-tier throughput, recording 6.89 million Redis SET operations per second, 6.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 74.83 GB/sec. Multi-core stress-ng tests reached 7235.59 points, though instruction-heavy encryption tasks showed limited throughput due to missing x86 instruction sets. The instance delivers solid cost efficiency for Arm-native applications requiring consistent non-burstable CPU compute, making it well-suited for web servers, microservices, lightweight caching layers, and containerized CI/CD builds.
